questions.q: What is the minimum common electrical circuit for a basic outdoor grill island?
questions.explanation: 20-amp GFCI is the typical residential minimum for an outdoor kitchen with lighting and a basic accessory outlet. Larger appliance combos need more.

questions.q: Why should quartz (engineered) generally not be used as an outdoor kitchen countertop?
choices: The resin binder yellows and cracks under UV and heat
questions.explanation: Engineered quartz uses a polymer resin that degrades under sustained UV and heat exposure. Granite, quartzite, and porcelain slab are the appropriate outdoor materials.

questions.q: When should countertop templating be done?
questions.explanation: Field variance always accumulates. Templating off the completed enclosure is the only way to get a countertop that fits.

questions.q: An LP tank feeding an outdoor kitchen must be located:
choices: Outside any enclosed space and typically at least ten feet from ignition sources per most codes
questions.explanation: LP tanks are pressurized flammable gas containers. Codes universally require them outside enclosed spaces at safe distances from ignition sources.

questions.q: Before pouring concrete or starting framing, what must be confirmed on the print?
choices: Utility rough-in stub locations from the licensed trade
questions.explanation: Missed stub locations mean saw-cutting finished stone or breaking concrete later. Confirming stub positions before build is the single most important coordination step.

questions.q: A gas grill under an enclosed roof requires:
choices: An outdoor-rated vent hood ducted outside, or approved free-air openings
questions.explanation: Combustion products accumulate under enclosed roofs. Code requires either mechanical ventilation (outdoor-rated hood ducted outside) or an open-air structure with adequate free-air openings.

questions.q: The correct leak-test method after connecting gas to an appliance is:
choices: Soap-water solution on joints or a manometer test
questions.explanation: Soap-water solution shows bubbles at any leak; a manometer holds the line at test pressure and reveals any pressure drop. Either is required per code.

questions.q: Yellow flames on a newly commissioned gas burner indicate:
choices: A supply problem that must be corrected before customer acceptance
The burner needs to break in
questions.explanation: Yellow flames indicate incomplete combustion — commonly a mismatched orifice for the gas type, poor air adjustment, or a partially blocked supply. Fix before accepting.

questions.q: When photographing utility rough-in, why three angles?
choices: To create a complete as-built record for future service and inspection
questions.explanation: Three angles capture stub locations, sizes, and label markings well enough that a future technician or inspector can reconstruct exactly what was installed.

questions.q: How long should the refrigerator run before customer delivery?
choices: 24 hours to confirm it holds temperature
questions.explanation: 24 hours confirms compressor performance, temperature stability, and that no in-transit damage prevents proper cooling — the standard commissioning check.
